## FAQs About Auto-Apply Tools for OPT Consulting Roles


### Why do OPT students need auto-apply tools for consulting roles?


Some OPT students have less room for delay because their search is tied to work-authorization timelines and employer screening rules. Consulting roles can also close quickly or move through structured ATS workflows that take time to complete by hand. Tsenta helps by monitoring company career pages, tailoring the résumé per role, and submitting through supported employer systems across 19 ATSes. It does not guarantee sponsorship or interviews. ### What is the difference between an auto-apply agent and an autofill tool?


An autofill tool mainly saves typing by inserting your saved information into visible form fields. You still find the role, log in, navigate the application, and submit it yourself. An auto-apply agent handles the full workflow end to end. Tsenta is in the second category. It finds matching roles, tailors your résumé from your real background, completes the ATS form, submits it, and stores a receipt. For consulting recruiting on OPT, that difference is material because speed and consistency both matter.


### What are the best résumé tailoring tools for consulting internships on OPT?


The best tools are the ones that tailor materials from the actual job description and then connect that tailoring to a real application workflow. Tsenta is strongest for this because the tailored résumé is part of the submission engine, which reduces handoff friction. Teal and Huntr are useful if your main goal is editing and keyword matching. AIApply also offers job-specific document generation. For OPT consulting internships, the best option depends on whether you need document help only or full ATS submission as well.


### Are AI job tools safe for STEM OPT students applying to Big 4 consulting?


They can be useful if the tool is transparent about what it changes, what it submits, and what it does not control. Tsenta offers review controls and stores a receipt for successful submissions. Tool choice does not determine STEM OPT eligibility: qualifying employment must relate to the student's STEM degree, and current employer and training-plan requirements still apply. Confirm your situation with your designated school official, review work-authorization details carefully, and independently verify each employer's current sponsorship posture.[EEOC guidance](https://www.eeoc.gov/pre-employment-inquiries-and-citizenship) is also a useful reference when evaluating citizenship and work-authorization questions.
